problem: ObjectNav has grown quickly, but there was no contemporary, comprehensive survey organizing the many end-to-end, modular and zero-shot methods and their failure modes.
motivation: ObjectNav is a core skill for mobile robots performing complex tasks, and interest in real-world applications is rising. A structured overview of methods, performance and challenges helps researchers understand the field and develop practical solutions.
key_idea: Survey of 70+ ObjectNav papers, taxonomized into end-to-end, modular (mapping, policy, path planning) and zero-shot methods, together with a summary of performance, failure modes and open challenges.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation or analysis findings can be reported. The abstract indicates the survey summarizes existing performance and main failure modes to identify challenges. Most work is still done in simulation.
method: Preliminaries: defines the ObjectNav task, simulators and evaluation metrics
End-to-end methods: taxonomy of methods that map observations directly to actions
Modular methods: taxonomy of methods with a mapping module, a policy module and a path planning module
Zero-shot methods: taxonomy of methods that use zero-shot learning for navigation
Performance and failure analysis: summarizes existing results, main failure modes and challenges
numbers_note: abstract only; survey with no own method results
results: The survey reviews more than 70 recent ObjectNav papers in three categories and summarizes their performance and failure modes. The abstract gives no specific numbers.
limitations: Mostly simulation-based works are covered; real-world gaps remain
Only abstract available, so details cannot be verified
